sbp_domain.conclusion:
The developers document an SBP range of 90-200 mmHg, not 90-180. I re-opened every primary source on 2026-10-09 and confirmed this.

1. **Developer paper.** Khan et al., Circulation 2024;149:430-449 (PMC10910659, DOI https://doi.org/10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.123.067626, full text via PubMed). Methods > Study Population excludes people with SBP <90 or >200 mm Hg, using the PCE cutoffs. Other limits there:
   - TC 130-320 mg/dL
   - HDL-C 20-100 mg/dL
   - BMI 18.5 to <40.0 kg/m2 (the PCP-HF range)
   - adults aged 30-79 without ASCVD or HF

   The main text gives no ranges for eGFR, UACR or HbA1c.

2. **Official AHA calculator.** I re-read app.bundle.js v=1.28.2.29416 in the browser.
   - SBP: placeholder "90-200", message "Systolic blood pressure must be between 90-200 mm Hg", validation rejects <90 or >200. The string "90-180" does not appear anywhere in the bundle.
   - Other limits: age 30-79, TC 130-320, HDL 20-100, BMI 18.5-39.9, eGFR 15-140, UACR 0-25000 mg/g (an entry of exactly "0" becomes 0.1), HbA1c 3-15%.
   - The AHA FAQ PDF (p.7 of 8) says missing or out-of-range required inputs produce no estimate. It suggests using the closest in-range value, which may over- or under-estimate risk.

3. **pyprevent (pinned commit 69f3414, v0.2.0).** It enforces SBP 90-200 (_core.py line 244). It is looser than the calculator on eGFR (>0), UACR (>=0) and HbA1c (>0). It gates CVD/ASCVD on TC/HDL and gates HF only on BMI 18.5 to <40.

4. **preventr (pinned commit ebe2ac1, v0.12.0).** The 90-180 bound comes from here. estimate_risk.R lines 410-419 say the equations "technically permit up to 200 mmHg"; the author capped SBP at 180 for clinical reasons (hypertensive urgency). This is roxygen documentation, not a code comment. His 4.5% HbA1c floor, against 3% in the calculator, is likewise his own choice.

**Corrections to the extraction:**
- The previous conclusion said the calculator page states that 30-year risk applies only to ages 30-59. The visible page text does not say this. The code shows 30-year results only when submittedAge <60 (offsets ~1518490-1523358). I added this as a separate item.
- The pyprevent README is not among the local pinned files. I read it from raw.githubusercontent.com at the pinned commit.
- I corrected several bundle offsets: SBP validation is at 510106 and 511762; the UACR 0-to-0.1 mapping is at ~453460-453560.
- I added the FAQ page number (p.7) and the full list of required variables from the FAQ.
- I added pyprevent's age-horizon mask and binary-input checks.
- I added a separate item for the supplement, marked unknown.

**Still unverified:**
- **Supplement:** not inspected. The files are docx/xlsx downloads, which the task forbids.
- **AHA's official R/STATA code:** AHAprevent / AHA-DS-Analytics/PREVENT is behind a license agreement, and both GitHub URLs return 404 without sign-in.

Neither of these affects the SBP answer: the paper and the AHA's own calculator agree on 200.

I fetched both PDFs and the JS bundle in memory inside the browser and saved nothing to disk.

**Recommendation:** use 90-200 mmHg as the developer-documented SBP domain. Treat 180 only as a stricter optional sensitivity bound, credited to preventr (Mayer), not to the AHA.

items.label: Lacher 2005: how CVw (CVI) was computed
items.value: The paper defines CVt = [(CVa)^2 + (CVw)^2]^1/2. This assumes all CVs are measured at the same analyte mean and that pre- and postanalytical variation is negligible. CVa equals the lab method imprecision (CVi) if there is no bias. Hence 'The CVw was calculated as [(CVt)^2 - (CVa)^2]^1/2'. CVi values come from the NHANES III laboratory procedures manual (ref 6). WP variation came from a nonrandom, unweighted repeat sample with a mean (SD) of 17 (8) days between the two measurements. Some distributions were non-Gaussian, so extreme outliers were removed by Tukey's method (more than 3 IQR below the 25th or above the 75th percentile). No log transformation is described; CVs are on the original scale. The paper does not say how CVt was estimated from the paired values.
items.location: Body paragraph 2 (CVt formula); paragraph 3 (CVi, ref 6); paragraph 5 ('The CVg values were estimated...', which gives the CVw formula and Tukey rule); Table 1 footnote 3 ('Outliers were deleted by the Tukey method')
items.note: Sample sizes: BP n = 24 978 and WP n = 2426 sample persons. The WP sample (about 10%) was recruited for roughly equal sex proportions, half aged 20-39 and half 40+. It was older than the BP sample (mean age 42.9 vs 30.8 y). Second exams were scheduled at the same time of day when possible. CVg came from a weighted Taylor-series analysis, with BP SD = (SE^2 + SDsrs^2)^1/2. Footnote 3 is attached to all six PREVENT-relevant rows, but not to albumin, apolipoprotein A, apolipoprotein B, bicarbonate, chloride, total protein, varicella antibody or vitamin A.

items.label: Selvin 2013: how CVw was computed
items.value: Selvin says 'The within-person coefficients of variation (CVw) were calculated using a standard approach' and cites ref 22: Juraschek SP et al., Clin Biochem 2012;45(9):694-6, PMID 22425605, PMC3575740, DOI 10.1016/j.clinbiochem.2012.02.027. Ref 22 defines CV = SD/mean, with SD = sqrt( sum_i (x_i - y_i)^2 / (2n) ) and mean = (sum x_i/n + sum y_i/n)/2. That is the root-mean-square of the uncentered pair differences over sqrt 2, divided by the grand mean. Selvin adds: 'Because urine albumin and urine creatinine are highly skewed, they were analyzed on the log scale.' CVw is total within-person variability ('includes biological and analytical variability'); CVa was not subtracted.
items.source: Selvin 2013 full text; Juraschek 2012 full text (ref 22)
items.location: Selvin: Methods, Statistical Analysis; abstract Measurements; Table 2 footnote. Juraschek: Materials and methods, CV equation
items.note: The log base is not stated, but log10 is strongly supported. With albumin in mg/L and creatinine in mg/dL, log10 ACR (mg/g) = log10 albumin - (log10 creatinine - 2) = 0.88 - 0.03 = 0.85, exactly the Table 2 log-ACR mean. No natural-log unit conversion gives this. Because the SD uses uncentered differences, any systematic Exam 1-Exam 2 shift adds to CVw, for example the cystatin C recalibration drift (mean difference -0.03 mg/L) and eGFRcys (+3.05). Table 2 footnote a says 'Range is shown in parentheses', but the Results text calls them 'confidence intervals' ('non-overlapping confidence intervals'). Selvin does not say how they were computed; Juraschek 2012 used bias-corrected bootstrap CIs with 1000 replications. Differences = Exam 1 minus Exam 2.

items.label: Selvin 2013: derived consistency check on the log-scale urine CVw (not a source value)
items.value: Applying ref 22's formula to Table 2's own columns, SDw = sqrt((SDd^2 + mean_d^2)/2) divided by the mean of the two exam means: log albumin 0.3748/0.875 = 42.8%; log urine creatinine 0.2263/2.03 = 11.1%; log ACR 0.3182/0.85 = 37.4%. The printed values are 37.3%, 43.0% and 11.3%: the same three numbers, but on permuted rows. The same calculation reproduces the eGFR rows exactly (MDRD 9.6, CKD-EPI cr 6.6, CKD-EPI cys 6.7) and the serum rows within about 0.3 points (creatinine 7.3 vs 7.6, cystatin C 6.5 vs 6.8, BTP 11.5 vs 11.6, B2M 8.1 vs 8.4). That validates the method.
items.location: Table 2, Difference (SD) and Exam 1/Exam 2 mean columns
items.note: The SD-of-difference column shows log ACR (0.45) varying more than log urine creatinine (0.32), contradicting the text's claim that ACR is much less variable than either part. Those SDs are internally consistent: the implied correlation of the albumin and creatinine differences is about 0.53. So the published 11.3% 'ACR CVw' is very likely a row-label permutation. In any case it is a CV of log10 values and depends on units. Derived original-scale equivalents, assuming log10: within-person SD of log10 ACR = 0.318 (0.733 ln units), giving CV = sqrt(exp(0.733^2) - 1) = 84%. Urine albumin is 105% and urine creatinine 56%. Recompute in the project's NHANES III data before using any of these.

lacher.conclusion:
I re-checked both papers against the primary sources myself. Every transcribed value in the extraction is correct. I made five corrections or downgrades and added one item.

**Sources I re-opened**
- **Lacher 2005** (Clin Chem 51:450-452; [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1373/clinchem.2004.039354), PMID 15590751): full text and Table 1 from the Wayback copies of the old clinchem.org site. My fresh copies are in scratchpad\verify_lacher. The current OUP page is a plain paywall, not a bot check.
- **Selvin 2013** (AJKD 61:716-722; [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1053/j.ajkd.2012.11.048), PMC3628297): full text via PubMed Central, with tables and references from NCBI's XML. My copy is scratchpad\verify_selvin\pmc.xml.
- **Juraschek 2012** (Selvin's ref 22; [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.clinbiochem.2012.02.027), PMC3575740): checked for the CV formula Selvin relies on.

**Lacher 2005**
- **Method:** CVw = sqrt(CVt² − CVa²), with CVa taken as the lab's method imprecision (CVi). Values are on the original scale, with no log transform. Outliers were removed by Tukey's rule (beyond 3 IQR). The repeat sample was nonrandom and unweighted, about 17 (SD 8) days apart.
- **PREVENT-relevant rows, all confirmed:**

| Analyte | CVw | CVa | WP n |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total cholesterol | 8.2% | 2.3% | 2299 |
| HDL cholesterol | 12.4% | 2.5% | 2266 |
| Serum creatinine | 6.8% | 1.0% | 2062 |
| HbA1c | 1.5% | 3.1% | 2195 |
| Plasma glucose | 8.3% | 1.7% | 1950 |
| Urine creatinine | 43.0% | 2.2% | 1626 |

- **Missing:** there is no urine albumin or ACR row among the 42 analytes.

**Lacher corrections and additions**
1. **Creatinine note relabelled:** that these are the original NHANES III Jaffe values (not recalibrated) is my inference from the 2004 date. The paper does not say so.
2. **Subtraction check widened to all 42 rows (my arithmetic, rated likely):**
   - 18 rows match the value after subtracting CVa.
   - 4 rows match the total CV before subtraction: total cholesterol, total calcium, TIBC and sodium.
   - 20 rows are ambiguous.
   - For PREVENT: cholesterol looks unsubtracted, and the text's own 0.079 is the subtracted value. HbA1c is clearly subtracted. Serum creatinine leans toward subtracted, not an even case as the earlier version said. HDL, glucose and urine creatinine cannot be decided.
3. **New item:** the text says CVw exceeded CVi for all analytes. The table contradicts this for albumin, ALP and HbA1c. So the 1.5% for HbA1c depends on subtracting a CVa larger than itself.

**Selvin 2013**
- **Method:** CVw is total within-person variation; analytical CV was not subtracted. The formula comes from Juraschek 2012: CV = SD/mean, with SD = sqrt(Σ(x−y)²/2n) on the raw differences and mean = the average of the two exam means. Because the differences are not mean-centred, a systematic shift between exams adds to CVw. That matters for cystatin C, which was assayed in 2006 and 2009.
- **Scale:** urine albumin and creatinine were analyzed on the log scale. The base is not stated, but log10 is supported by the table itself: 0.88 − (2.03 − 2) = 0.85, exactly the log-ACR mean.
- **Brackets after each CVw:** footnoted as a "range", but the Results text calls them confidence intervals. Selvin doesn't say how they were computed; Juraschek used a bias-corrected bootstrap.
- **Values, all confirmed:**

| Measure | CVw | n |
|---|---|---|
| Serum creatinine (standardized) | 7.6% (7.2–8.0) | 795 |
| Cystatin C | 6.8% (6.4–7.3) | 795 |
| Log urine albumin | 37.3% (34.4–40.1) | 1294 |
| Log urine creatinine | 43.0% (39.8–46.3) | 1294 |
| Log ACR | 11.3% (10.7–11.9) | 1294 |

- **Exclusions:** 26 people with values more than 3 SD from the mean were dropped from the serum analysis, taking it from 821 to 795. No urine exclusions are listed.

**The ACR problem (my arithmetic, rated likely):** Selvin's formula, applied to Table 2's own columns, reproduces the three eGFR rows exactly and the serum rows within about 0.3 points. Applied to the urine rows, it gives:
- 42.8% for log albumin,
- 11.1% for log urine creatinine,
- 37.4% for log ACR.

That is the printed set of values on the wrong rows. So the 11.3% "ACR CVw" is very likely mislabelled, and it is also unit-dependent. My derived original-scale CVs are about 84% for ACR, 105% for albumin and 56% for urine creatinine. Recompute in the project data rather than cite Selvin's 11.3%.

**Connector status:** four PubMed-related connectors (biorender, owkin, synapse, wiley) need authorizing in claude.ai connector settings or via /mcp before they can be used. The research-desk reference-lookup server failed to connect; I didn't need it for this check.

cva.conclusion:
I re-opened every primary source myself:
- **labman.pdf:** fetched into memory from wwwn.cdc.gov and text-extracted with my own script; selected raw pages also saved.
- **lab-acc.pdf and LABSE-acc.pdf:** re-extracted page by page from the local files.
- **Selvin 2013 and Miller 2010:** full text via PubMed/PMC.
- **Lacher 2005:** Internet Archive copies of the clinchem.org Table 1 and full-text pages.
- **CDC LSP page:** WebFetch.
- **EFLM BV database:** its API plus the rendered meta_calculations page.

All labman values, page numbers, Selvin values and EFLM meta-analysis CVIs in the extraction are confirmed.

**Corrections:**
1. **Lacher 2005 is accessible.** Its status changes from unknown to verified (full text). Table 1 'Method CVi, %' gives NHANES-specific imprecision, which the paper says equals CVa when there is no bias:

   | Analyte | Lacher CVi | labman QC tables |
   |---|---|---|
   | Total cholesterol | 2.3% | 1.25-1.33% |
   | HDL-C | 2.5% | 2.49% (AQ13) |
   | Serum creatinine | 1.0% | 2.0-2.7% |
   | Urine creatinine | 2.2% | no table |
   | Plasma glucose | 1.7% | 1.6-2.2% |
   | Glycohemoglobin | 3.1% | 1.57-1.73% |

   There is no urine albumin row. Lacher cites labman but does not say which table each value comes from. HDL-C and glucose agree with labman; total cholesterol, creatinine and HbA1c do not, so report both. Lacher's CVw values (TC 8.2, HDL 12.4, creatinine 6.8, urine creatinine 43.0, glucose 8.3, GHb 1.5%) are biological CVs with the analytical part removed.
2. **The EFLM urine BIVAC grades were wrong.** The earlier agent read the 'scale' field, which scores BIVAC item 1 only, as the overall grade. The real grades ('score_display') are:
   - Howey 1987 and Kong 2022: C.
   - Hofmann & Guder 1989 and Shephard 1981: D.
   - Çalık & Şeneş 2023: B (correct before).
   - No urine albumin or urine creatinine dataset is graded A.
   - I also added the missing healthy-adult datasets: Howey 5060, 5061 and 5063, and Ricós 1994.
3. **CDC LSP:** the mmol/L table prints '0.03 (RV)' for total cholesterol, which settles the earlier ambiguity: the limit is SD ≤ 0.03×RV, i.e. CV ≤3%. Lacher's text confirms the NCEP total-cholesterol criterion (<3% imprecision). The HDL ≤4% goal is labelled NCEP only by context in Miller 2010, so it stays 'likely'.

**Recommended CVa for the table:**

| Analyte | Primary value (source) | Alternative / note |
|---|---|---|
| Total cholesterol | 1.25-1.33% (labman Table 8, VII-Q-16) | Lacher 2.3% |
| HDL-C | 2.49% (AQ13 pool, labman Table 8) | Lacher 2.5% |
| Serum creatinine | 2.0-2.7% (labman Hitachi 737 Table 3; Selvin gives the same) | Lacher 1.0% |
| HbA1c | 1.57-1.73% (labman Table 5, VII-O-11) | data-file note '2.0'; Lacher 3.1% |
| Plasma glucose | 1.6-2.2% (labman Table 3, VII-M-8) | Lacher 1.7% |
| Urine albumin | 4.8-16.1% (Selvin 2013) | labman gives only a ≤10% acceptance limit |
| Urine creatinine | 1.5-7.7% (Selvin; pool units probably mmol/L) | Lacher 2.2% |

NCEP and CDC values are goals only.

**Flags in the sources:**
- The Q20 mean differs between Table 7 (261) and Table 8 (213).
- The AQ13 within-run CV (7.73%) is larger than its total CV (2.49%), which is impossible, so it is probably a typo.

items.value: The Circulation correction (Circulation 2014;129(25 Suppl 2):S74-S75) lists 12 changes. Item 3: 'Appendixes have been reordered and renumbered' so that the author and reviewer RWI tables come first as Appendixes 1 and 2. Item 12 refers to 'Appendix 3, (Appendix 6 in published document)', which confirms a +3 shift. None of the 12 items changes any Table A or Table B value; the only table change is item 6, which edits Table 4, the recommendations table.

items.location: Correction items 1-12; item 3 is the renumbering, item 6 is Table 4, item 12 gives the Appendix 3 → 6 mapping.
items.note: The PMC/JACC manuscript keeps the pre-renumbering order: App 2 = CQ2 evidence statements, App 4 = PCE development, App 7 = abbreviations. Circulation has App 5 = CQ2, App 7 = PCE, App 3 = abbreviations. This is consistent with the PCE tables being Appendix 4 in PMC and Appendix 7 in Circulation.

items.label: Equation / how to compute (Table B)
items.value: Risk = 1 - S10^exp(IndX'B - MeanX'B). IndX'B is the individual's sum of coefficient × value, and MeanX'B is the race- and sex-specific overall mean of that sum. Age, total cholesterol, HDL-C and SBP are entered as natural logs. Age interactions are ln(age) × ln(lipid or SBP), or ln(age) × the smoker indicator. Only the treated or the untreated SBP term is used, whichever matches the patient. Worked example (white men): '1 − 0.9144^e(60.69–61.18)' 'equates to a 5.3% probability'.
items.location: Circulation Appendix 7, Table B (text table). PMC4700825 Appendix 4, Table B (T12).
items.note: In the Circulation HTML the formula is rendered '1 − S10(lndX’B–MeanX’B)', with the superscript e missing. The PMC XML renders it '1−S10e(IndX'B−MeanX'B)'. Correction to the earlier note: both versions say the profile is 'provided in Table 5', but it is actually in Table A. This is an internal mislabel. It is NOT inherited verbatim from the NHLBI Work Group Report, whose own Table 5 text says the profile is 'provided in tables 4a and 4b'.

items.label: Table A footnotes (meaning of N/A and dash; Coefficient × Value definition)
items.value: Footnote *: 'Defined as first occurrence of nonfatal myocardial infarction or CHD death, or fatal or nonfatal stroke.' Footnote †: Coefficient × Value is the natural log of the value multiplied by the parameter estimate for age, lipids and BP. For age interactions, ln(age) is multiplied by ln(lipid or BP) and then by the parameter estimate. The † footnote also says that 'N/A' means the covariate was not included in the model for that sex–race group, and that '—' means the value was not used in the example (the example used untreated rather than treated SBP).
items.location: Circulation Appendix 7, Table A footnotes * and †. PMC4700825 Table A (T11) footnotes * and †.

pce.conclusion:
I re-checked every item against the primary sources myself. All the requested values are confirmed. I made a few corrections to the notes, but none to the numbers.

**What I re-read**
- **Circulation:** the open-access HTML of Goff DC Jr et al., Circulation 2014;129(25 Suppl 2):S49-S73 ([doi:10.1161/01.cir.0000437741.48606.98](https://doi.org/10.1161/01.cir.0000437741.48606.98), PMID 24222018), read in the browser pane. The equations are in **Appendix 7**, Table A (coefficients, means, baseline survivals and the worked example) and Table B (method and formula). The table of contents gives the appendix's start page as S71.
- **PMC:** the Circulation version has no PMC copy (PubMed returns no PMCID for 24222018). The PMC copy is the JACC co-publication, an NIH author manuscript ([doi:10.1016/j.jacc.2013.11.005](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jacc.2013.11.005), PMID 24239921, PMC4700825, NIHMS633784). I re-fetched its XML, and according to PubMed's PMC record the same tables appear there as Table A (T11) and Table B (T12) in **Appendix 4**. Every cell matches the Circulation version.
- **Correction notice:** the Circulation correction ([doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000067](https://doi.org/10.1161/CIR.0000000000000067)) renumbered the appendixes. That explains Appendix 4 in PMC versus Appendix 7 in Circulation. None of its 12 items changes a value in Table A or Table B.
- **NHLBI Work Group Report:** I re-fetched the PDF and extracted its text. Its Tables 4a and 4b (report pages 14-15) match the guideline in every value, with the minus signs confirmed.

**Values confirmed**
- All 13 coefficients for each of the four groups. Where a term is not in a group's model, I recorded it as N/A (marked N/A in the table) or "row absent" (no such row in the men's section).
- Mean (coefficient × value): white women −29.18, African American women 86.61, white men 61.18, African American men 19.54.
- Baseline survival S10: 0.9665, 0.9533, 0.9144, 0.8954 in the same order.
- The example person (age 55, total cholesterol 213 mg/dL, HDL 50 mg/dL, untreated SBP 120 mm Hg, nonsmoker, no diabetes), with the ln values the table uses: age 4.01, age² 16.06, TC 5.36, age×TC 21.48, HDL 3.91, age×HDL 15.68, SBP 4.79, age×SBP 19.19.
- The coefficient × value terms, individual sums (−29.67, 86.16, 60.69, 18.97) and risks (2.1%, 3.0%, 5.3%, 6.1%). Section 4 of the guideline repeats the four risks in its text.

**Corrections and additions**
1. **The "Table 5" mislabel.** Table B says the example profile is "provided in Table 5", but it is in Table A. The earlier note said this was copied from the NHLBI report. It wasn't: the report's own text points to its Tables 4a and 4b.
2. **Rounding in the printed terms.** Recomputing from full-precision logs, four printed terms are 0.01 off: white women ln age² (78.43 vs printed 78.44), white women ln age×ln TC (−66.90 vs −66.91), white men ln age×ln TC (−57.23 vs −57.24) and African American women ln age×ln untreated SBP (−116.78 vs −116.79). The earlier extraction caught only two of these. The white men's printed terms also add up to 60.70, while the printed individual sum is 60.69.
3. **Risks from full-precision inputs.** These give 2.05%, 3.03%, 5.38% and 6.07%. The printed 5.3% for white men only comes out if you use the rounded sum of 60.69; full precision would round to 5.4%.
4. **NHLBI report details.** Its example column prints the raw values (55, 213, 50, 120), not the ln values. Its Table 5 text wrongly says SBP 124 mm Hg and current smoker. Use the guideline's version.
5. **Not checked.** I did not confirm the exact print page of Table A (it must fall within S71-S73) or of the Section 4 paragraph (the section starts at S55).
